chunks: Reducing the measurement ground loop. The question: How can you reduce your ground loop?
To reduce the ground loop in a measurement, you make it shorter and smaller.
Remove the long clip lead and use a spring ground tip or the probe barrel touching a ground pad right next to the signal. Better probes and sockets help further.
Then check that the picture does not change when you shorten the loop more.
Think of shortening a leash. A long, loose leash lets a dog wander and swing wildly with every tug. A short leash keeps it tight. The probe's ground lead is the leash.
Pulling it tight to the ground pad stops the wild swinging, which is ringing, and also shrinks the area of the loop, which catches stray noise the way a hoop catches rain.
The point is the same each time: keep the return path short and close to the signal.
Four attack routes. The first two are the same action (a short, close ground connection) viewed in two ways: lower inductance and less area.
Spring ground tip: a short spring that contacts ground right beside the probe tip. Tip-and-barrel: touching the probe's metal barrel against ground instead of using a lead.
Ground pad: a pad connected to ground, placed next to a test point.
Differential probe: a probe that measures the difference between two points without using the scope's ground lead.
Noise-floor check: shorting the tip to ground to see how much noise the setup itself adds.
Replace a 150 nanohenries clip lead with a 10 nanohenries spring tip.
With 10 picofarads of probe capacitance and a 50 ohms source, the ringing moves from about 130 megahertz to about 500 megahertz.
The overshoot (the signal swinging past its true level) falls from about 52 % to about 2 %. Then do the check: short the tip to ground at the pad and look at the noise.
Shorten the loop again and see whether the waveform changes. When it stops changing, the loop is small enough. That is the whole idea.

"I'd shrink the loop in order of effectiveness: remove the long clip and use a spring ground tip or tip-and-barrel; ground at the nearest quiet ground pad, which I design in next to test points with vias to the plane; use soldered leads, SMA connectors or low-capacitance active probes for fast signals; and use differential or isolated probes for floating nodes.
For mains loops, one earth point or isolation, never lifting the safety earth. Then verify with a shorted-tip noise-floor check."
